title: Read through a window
starter:
let window (data : int list) (off : int) (k : int) : int list =
  []
hints: Do the check first. The window fits when `off >= 0` and `off + k <= List.length data`. If it does not fit, `invalid_arg "out of bounds"` raises the right exception.
The window covers positions `off`, `off + 1` and so on, up to but not including `off + k`.
`List.filteri (fun i _ -> i >= off && i < off + k) data` keeps exactly the elements at those positions.

answer.explain: The solution checks `off < 0 || off + k > List.length data` and raises `Invalid_argument "out of bounds"` when the window does not fit. Otherwise it keeps the elements whose position `i` has `off <= i < off + k`. The check comes first because a window that runs past the end must be refused, not cut short.
